cases.question: How do I make Le Tourin garlic soup?

response.answer: Le Tourin is a garlic soup from the village of Le Fleix in Dordogne, serving 2 and taking about 30 minutes. Steps: 1. In a frying pan, brown the chopped garlic in the olive oil. 2. Add the flour, mix well, then cook for a few minutes to remove the floury taste. 3. Gradually stir in the water and cook for 10 minutes. 4. Beat the egg white in a small bowl, gradually whisk in a ladleful of the soup to temper it, then stir the mixture back into the soup pot. 5. Combine the egg yolk, pepper and vinegar in a small bowl, then gradually temper the yolks with a ladleful of soup. 6. Remove the soup from the heat, stir in the egg yolk mixture and season to taste with salt. 7. Place thin slices of bread in each soup bowl, pour the soup on top and serve hot. Ingredients: 10–12 cloves garlic chopped, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 tablespoon flour, 4 cups water or as needed, 1 egg separated, pepper to taste, 1 teaspoon vinegar, salt to taste. The ingredient list comes from the source page and may be incomplete. Another version exists: the notes say you can optionally use an equal mixture of chopped onions and garlic.

cases.question: What's the method for pasta carbonara?

response.answer: The first recipe provided, Spaghetti alla Carbonara, gives this method for six servings. Dice 225–500 g of guanciale or pancetta into 2.5 cm pieces. Bring a big pot of water to a boil and salt it when it begins to simmer. Cook 450 g spaghetti until al dente, then drain it, reserving 1 cup of the water. While the pasta cooks, heat 3–4 tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the pancetta and cook about 10 minutes over low heat until most of the fat has rendered but it is still chewy and barely browned. In a bowl, slowly whisk about ½ cup of the pasta water into 5 egg yolks, then add 178 ml each of grated Pecorino Romano and Parmigiano-Reggiano and mix thoroughly with a fork. Transfer the drained spaghetti immediately to the skillet, toss, and turn off the heat. Add the egg and cheese mixture while stirring in the remaining pasta water to thin the sauce and create an emulsion. Finish with ½ tablespoon of freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. A variant, Carbonara Pasta, uses 4 eggs, fresh pancetta, thyme, onion and lemon zest, mixed in a bowl rather than a skillet; its ingredient list comes from the source page and may be incomplete. Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon peel, pour the mixture into a 2-quart (1.9 L) casserole and allow it to cool, then sprinkle with cinnamon powder.
